platform.note: the original CARE training used 2 Torch threads on macOS; the reference here is regenerated on this platform with 1 thread and deterministic algorithms

inputs.location: artifacts/ (gitignored; CARE-derived data and trained state are not committed to the public repository)
inputs.batches: FrozenPreparation(prepared=care-train-profile-schedule-20261016, dataset=care-numeric-input-20261016, fold=0).batch(step): 8 train-prefix examples, context [8,3,128], actual [8,3,32]; steps 0 and 4095 must equal fold-0-batch-reference.bin byte for byte
inputs.state: the selected fold0 state (step 4096): 59 trainable tensors and the buffers scale_floor, position, time_mask; AdamW step and first/second moments for the mature case

recipe.loss: small_model.training_loss: pinball on normalized quantiles against (actual - context_center) / context_scale, mean over B*C*H*3
recipe.optimizer: AdamW lr 3e-4, betas [0.9, 0.999], eps 1e-8, weight_decay 0.01, decoupled, no amsgrad, foreach/fused off, constant lr (no scheduler)

cases.one_update: selected parameters, fresh AdamW (step 0, zero moments), one update on batch step 0
cases.eight_updates: selected parameters, fresh AdamW, eight updates on batch steps 0..7 in order
cases.resume: Rust only, same backend and threads: continuous eight_updates versus 4 updates, checkpoint write, separate-process restore, 4 updates; byte-exact parameters, moments, counters and the final loss
cases.mature_import: selected parameters with the saved AdamW step 4096 and moments, one update on batch step 0 (the 4096-step schedule ends at step 4096, so the import update uses the first schedule batch, fixed here before any run)

compare.loss: every update: normalized_loss for update 1, eight_step_loss for later updates
compare.gradients: every update, all 59 tensors: raw and clipped under the R0.1 gradient rule, plus global norm and clip coefficient
compare.parameters: after update 1 (one_step_parameter) and after update 8 (eight_step_parameter) of eight_updates, after one_update and after mature_import (one_step_parameter); judged only on elements whose reference clipped |gradient| >= 1e-7 (K=10, eps 1e-8) at every update of that run up to the compared one; mature_import uses only its own update
compare.moments: first_moment and second_moment on all elements after each compared update
compare.forward: recorded after each compared update (normalized quantiles of the next batch, or of the last batch after the last update), judged only through the next update's loss

reference.generator: Torch float32 on this platform, run and hashed before any Rust run; saved under artifacts/, only hashes and summaries are committed
reference.independent_check: the same procedure in float64; the float32 reference is kept only if loss and gradients agree with float64 within R0.1 (parameters and moments are recorded, not gated, in this check)

records: per compared update: excluded parameter elements as a fraction of 109024, with tensor names and indices
every failing element with reference and Rust values
resources: wall time and peak memory per process

stop.exclusion: if more than 10% of parameter elements are excluded at any compared update, stop and investigate before accepting the result
stop.failure: any numeric failure is recorded and stops formal R2; no fixture, tolerance or reference change after Rust results exist
stop.harness: a failure before any numeric comparison exists (build, I/O, missing file) may be fixed and the run repeated; once Rust numeric results exist they are final
stop.limits: parent 900 s, child 870 s, peak memory 2 GiB per process, jobs 1

not_in_scope: validation selection, calibration, CARE test prediction or evaluation, further training, other folds, R3
